text: A new day dawns.
You brew a pot of tea and settle into your desk. The others haven't arrived yet—the silence is so deep you can almost hear the tea leaves drifting in the hot water.
Here, it matters little if you are late. After all, who dares to pass judgment on the dead?
For the employees of this office, there is no longer any need to conceal their desires. To crave sleep, to crave food… these are nothing but instinct.
Who could repeat the same task countless times and still love it? You sit here without holidays, sifting through files day after day, stripped of all feeling.
And here you are, seeking only to drink a cup of hot tea in the morning.
Come to think of it, you no longer remember how you arrived here. It feels as though, from the moment your consciousness was born, you have already been here—day after day, sifting through files.
Chatter, sifting through files, interrogating, deciding. Chatter, sifting through files, interrogating, deciding. Chatter, sifting through files, interrogating, deciding…
Day after day, in this place where no day truly exists.
Hey, good morning! No tea for me?
The silence was broken by a voice, and at the doorway appeared a familiar figure.
That expression… looks like I've disrupted your peaceful morning, huh?
You came here… just for my tea?
What a petty thought! I clearly came to give you some company.
None for you. This is a rare tea I've managed to get for myself.
You're surprisingly stingy, Your Excellency!
I'll give you a little.
You take a dusty goblet from the cabinet, shake off the dust, and pour it half full with tea.
You don't mind, I assume?
Of course not… mmm, it smells amazing!
Is there something you need for today?
I was just feeling a bit bored this morning… there's no sunlight here, so I can't even get a little sun…
You're about the only one left who still says good morning.
You seem a bit out of it today, huh?
Do you even remember how to work?
I come here to watch almost every day — I've memorized the whole process by now. I might even know it better than you.
All you really do is chat with people who come in to apply for Heaven, check and fill out their files, and then pick the one who fits the criteria best… and send them on their way.
What a leisurely job… and you even get all the gossip!
Truth be told, I don't really care much for this job.
Here's a little tip—during breaks, you can go have tea and chat with the applicants. Who knows, it might even help you make better decisions!
Sounds like a good idea. People relax more over tea… and I can even sneak out for a little break myself.
Work starts soon, so don't mess up!
And don't get too carried away with your feelings—after all, everyone here…
Never mind. There's no point in saying all this.
Are you submitting an application today as well?
Mm, you decide.
You open the file of your old friend.
This file is almost entirely blank. Even if no material was collected, shouldn't you at least remember your own name?
I really don't remember.
I thought you seemed a bit distracted today—so it would be a perfect timing for me. Too bad, too bad.
Gather more information if you like. There's no limit on the number of applications here, so there's no need to rush.
He smiles and drains the tea on the table in one gulp, wincing at the heat.
The tea is really hot!
It's fine, it's fine! I won't bother you at work then. I'll come back to submit my application once I've gathered all the information.
He stands up and leaves. He is a truly leisurely person.
His figure moves back and forth outside the door, greeting passersby along the way.

What a stubborn one… why does he come here to cause trouble every single day? Wandering around the office entrance, making everyone think we run a kindergarten, said a colleague who had just arrived at the office.
You sigh, silently wishing he would gather more information—if only… to remember who he is.
Without memory, without bonds, our souls are utterly impoverished.
You put the tea set away; it's time for you to start work.
